clue.text: Faulty car-dial sweeping

indicators.note: something faulty is out of order, so the letters of car-dial must be set out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that the dial in a car is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faulty' rearranges the seven letters of CAR-DIAL; the hyphen is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical reforms are sweeping ones, thorough and far-reaching.

clue.text: Devil-may-care airmen angle over water

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is a body of airmen
to angle over water is to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: A carefree pilot spending his leave fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's air arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffish person is rakish and unconventional, living with a careless disregard for propriety.

clue.text: Lexicologist's, not gunsmith's, description of a Lee-Enfield

definitions.text: Lexicologist's, not gunsmith's, description of a Lee-Enfield

parts.words: Lexicologist's, not gunsmith's, description of a Lee-Enfield
parts.note: the Lee-Enfield is a rifle, but a student of words sees a hyphenated name joining Lee and Enfield, the term used for such surnames

explanation.surface: A distinction between how a word expert and a gun maker would describe a famous British rifle.
explanation.walkthrough: A gunsmith would describe a shotgun with two barrels this way; the Lee-Enfield rifle has one barrel, but its name is a hyphenated pair, the way a lexicologist would use the term.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphenated surname joining two family names is called this, like a gun with two barrels.

clue.text: Top Wimbledon player, we hear, to resign

indicators.note: says the word for a top player is spoken, and a word with that sound is entered instead

parts.note: a top tennis player at a tournament such as Wimbledon is ranked as a seed

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that the leading tennis star is giving up.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship, where the leading players are seeded.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or surrender something, as one does on resigning a post or a game.

clue.text: Belonging to the side, all tear about

indicators.note: here signals the letters of all tear are moved about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A team fanatic who rushes around wildly on behalf of their side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to the side or flank of something, from the Latin for side.

clue.text: Easily-folded piano subject

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
subject to something means liable to it

explanation.surface: A piano that folds up conveniently for carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliable bends readily without breaking, so it is easily folded.

clue.text: Saw traveller in lead

indicators.note: says the word for a traveller sits inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
a rover is someone who travels about

explanation.surface: A wanderer who takes the lead in some venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same as an adage.

clue.text: This month is short, in a way short

parts.note: taken as written
St, short for street, is an abbreviated way or road

explanation.surface: A remark that the current month feels brief in one sense or another.
explanation.walkthrough: Inst., short for instant, is old business-letter usage for 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation inst. in formal letters refers to the current calendar month.

clue.text: They expand our airways old or short cabin components being replaced

indicators.note: the pieces of old or short cabin are replaced in new positions, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A cramped, outdated aircraft cabin being refitted by an airline.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests airlines and aircraft parts; the definition is medical, the airways of the lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: These drugs widen the bronchial tubes, easing breathing for asthma patients.

clue.text: 0 is one such small amount

definitions.meaning: the printed 0 stands for the letter O, the chemical symbol for oxygen, one of the substances in the periodic table
a trace or touch of something, as in a hint of truth

explanation.surface: A digit described as a tiny quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxygen is one of the chemical substances in the periodic table, and the word also means a small trace of something.

clue.text: Discovered at No.10, new sonnet-did VIP set it, originally?

parts.note: something discovered has been found
taken as written
the figures 1 and 0 of the number ten are read as the letters I and O

indicators.note: signals the letters of the pieces are made new, rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A poem found at Downing Street, wondering whether some dignitary arranged it.
explanation.walkthrough: No.10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence; here its number 10 is read as the letters IO. 'new' rearranges IO plus SONNET into IONSTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dignitary traditionally lays the first block at the start of building work, marking the ceremony.

clue.text: Troubles in mill starting up

indicators.note: the answer lies within the words mill starting, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Difficulties when a mill begins operating.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are misfortunes or problems, the plural of a noun for harm.

clue.text: Condensed cheese, strong

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
f, forte, is the musical direction meaning loud or strong

explanation.surface: A powerful cheese that has been concentrated.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief account is short and concise, cut down to essentials.

clue.text: Youth's trouble-spots?

parts.note: reads like places where young people cause trouble, but the spots are pimples on a teenage face

explanation.surface: Areas where young people cause disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: This skin condition brings pimples, a common affliction of adolescence.

clue.text: Disapproved of cricketer returning with a pair

indicators.note: says the word for the cricketer comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
in cricket a pair is two scores of nought in a match, so two Os

explanation.surface: A batsman coming back to the pavilion after two noughts, much to the disapproval of fans.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman is often called a bat, and 'a pair' means out for nought in both innings, written as two noughts.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo subject is one forbidden or frowned upon by social custom.

clue.text: Perhaps making granny extremely testy in Gateshead

indicators.note: takes the letters at the extremes, the first and last, of testy

parts.note: taken as written
read as Gate's head, the first letter of Gate, which is G

explanation.surface: A grandmother getting irritable in the town of Gateshead.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny is a kind of knot, so 'making granny' is tying a knot. Gateshead is a town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny knot is something you form by knotting, so the act of making one is an example of knotting.

clue.text: Head of hawk sort of albino -it has a broad head

indicators.note: takes the first letter, the head, of hawk
signals albino is turned into a sort of version of itself, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A white bird of prey with a wide head.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobnail is a short nail with a broad top, used to stud boot soles.

clue.text: Ban lad going to bed on time

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A boy being sent to bed punctually as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott is to refuse dealings with someone, shunning or excluding them.

clue.text: Shelter the saloon left

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car with an enclosed body
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A drinker leaving the bar to find cover.
explanation.definitionFit: This open-sided structure provides cover for a parked vehicle.

clue.text: Big race form by Olympic finalists

parts.note: a form is a school class

indicators.note: the final letters of Olympic, its last pair, come at the end

explanation.surface: A major contest whose form is decided by the last athletes in an Olympic event.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a school year group is a form. The classic races are the five great English flat races, such as the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: The classics are the major English flat horse races, such as the Derby and the Oaks.

clue.text: Experienced actor spouting pure rot

indicators.note: letters gushing out in a jumble, so pure rot is rearranged

explanation.surface: A veteran performer talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouper is a seasoned performer, especially one who carries on reliably despite difficulties.

clue.text: Suomi terminal, say

indicators.note: signals the word for terminal is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: something terminal is the end, the finish

explanation.surface: A remark about the last stop in Finland.
explanation.walkthrough: Suomi is the native name of Finland and its language.
explanation.definitionFit: Suomi is the name for the language of Finland in that language itself.

clue.text: Member's distal part that does not include the humorous, we hear

definitions.text: Member's distal part that does not include the humorous, we hear

parts.words: Member's distal part that does not include the humorous, we hear
parts.note: a limb's far section, below the elbow, lacking the upper-arm bone whose name sounds like humorous

explanation.surface: A body part described as having no sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: The humerus is the upper-arm bone; 'humorous, we hear' gives its sound, and the lower arm lies beyond it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower part of a limb, from elbow to wrist, lies beyond the upper-arm bone.

clue.text: Only cha stirred can bring such happy days

definitions.note: the clue words describe days; the answer is the adjective used before days

indicators.note: tea is stirred, and so are the letters of only cha, mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cup of tea, given a stir, is all you need for a good day.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha (char) is British slang for tea, fitting 'stirred' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are a past time of peace and contentment, a golden age.

clue.text: Live in these days, like retired people

indicators.note: says the word for live goes inside the abbreviation for these days

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Advice on modern living for pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like pensioners, but here it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has turned in for the night is lying in bed.

clue.text: Council accommodation?

definitions.meaning: a group that runs an organisation, as a committee does

explanation.surface: Housing provided by the local authority.
explanation.walkthrough: Council accommodation in Britain is public housing, the false trail here.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a governing committee and also the food supplied with lodgings.

clue.text: Bad weather there is trouble at hospital

indicators.note: puts the word for trouble next to the hospital abbreviation

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Storms causing difficulties at the local hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail is frozen precipitation falling as ice pellets, a form of unpleasant weather.

clue.text: Some undervalued spirit of lorry-drivers

indicators.note: only some of the letters of undervalued are taken, a run from within it

explanation.surface: Truck drivers' morale is underrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' here means fuel, not morale. Derv is the British name for diesel fuel for road vehicles; a lorry is a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: This diesel oil powers trucks, the name standing for diesel-engined road vehicle.

clue.text: After time, everybody is high

indicators.note: puts the word for everybody following the time abbreviation

parts.note: everybody means all

explanation.surface: Eventually everyone gets intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tall stands at a great height, lofty.

clue.text: Pal? Foe? Lax sentry con fused, that is so obvious

indicators.note: printed split, these words read as confused: the guard is muddled, and so are the letters of pal, foe, lax and sentry

explanation.surface: A careless sentry who cannot tell friend from enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that needs no further explanation is clear and plain on its face.

clue.text: What makes a body declare with a knave?

indicators.note: puts the word for knave together with the word for declare

parts.note: a knave is a rogue, a cad
to aver is to declare or assert

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a card player calls with a jack in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a card game, declaring with a knave (a jack); here knave means a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a dead body, especially one used for dissection.

clue.text: Old curse from N. Somali?

indicators.note: the answer is formed from the letters of N. Somali, made from them by reordering

explanation.surface: A hex originating with a northern Somali.
explanation.definitionFit: Malison is an archaic word for a curse, the opposite of benison.
